# dsh-plugin-backup
English | 中文

A backup plugin for DeepSeek Harness: it packages `$DSH_HOME` into verifiable,
restorable, downloada

ble archives by category, and can mirror those backups to
GitHub. Everything is available from three

faces that share one engine and one
single-run lock: the **Web settings page**, the **model tool su

rface**, and a
**CLI session**.

- Naming: `dsh-backup-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHmmss>`
- Categories: `settings`, `skills`, `plugins`, `sessions`

, `storages`
- Per backup: **download / verify / restore / delete**
- Settings: **backup path**, **b

ackup interval**, per-category switches, retention count,
verify-after-create, per-category archive

ceiling, GitHub sync
- No build step and no third-party runtime dependency: the host half is plain E

SM,
the browser half is a hand-writable CommonJS factory the shell loads as-is
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The Desktop app manages its own `desktop` profile: install through its plugin
manager (or `dsh plugi
n --profile desktop add …`) and restart the app.

`dsh plugin add` both records the dependency and appends the package name to
`dsh.profile.bundles` (

one composition layer). Reload or restart the Web
interface afterwards, then open **Settings → Data

sition layer). Reload or restart the Web
interface afterwards, then open **Settings → Data backup**.

> **Runtime support.** The plugin targets the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7 and 0.2.0
> lines: `peerDepen

dencies` declare `^0.1.7-rc.2 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` for `dsh-tools`
> and `dsh-typert-protocol`, and `engi

nes.dsh` mirrors that window. This matters
> on 0.2.0, whose boot performs a compatibility preflight

against the running
> runtime and **refuses to install or mount a bundle whose dsh peers it cannot

> satisfy** — an exact pin to one rc would be rejected. The two branches are not
> cosmetic: package

managers resolve with npm's prerelease rule, under which a
> prerelease is admitted only when some

comparator pins its exact version tuple,
> so one `>=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.3.0` window silently drops `0.2.0

-rc.1` and
> `0.2.0-rc.2` and fails `npm install` with `ERESOLVE`. Keep the window in
> `package.jso
n` in step with the APIs the plugin actually uses.

> A `file:` install is a **snapshot**: the profile keeps its own copy, so after
> changing this pack

age's source you must `dsh plugin --profile web remove <name>`
> and add it again. The measured veri

fication log lives in
> docs/verify.md.

> This is a DSH plugin, not a plain dependency: the host half injects the `tools`
> service declared

in its schema, and the browser half is discovered through the
> `dsh.client` declaration in `packag

e.json`. Without `$DSH_HOME` the plugin falls
> back to `~/.dsh`; in a non-Web profile (no `webServe

r` service) only *download*
> is unavailable — every other feature and tool still works.
## The page
Settings → **Data backup**:
| Block | Contents |
| Backup settings | Backup path (empty = `C:\Users\<user>\dsh_backups` on Windows, `~/dsh_backups` e
lsewhere; `~` and `${DSH_HOME}` are expanded), interval (off / 15 min / hourly / 6 h / daily / weekl

y), backups to keep, verify right after creating |
| Backup categories | The **selection** for a run
: check the categories to include, with select-all / select-none; the button names the current choic

e ("Back up now (3 categories)") and is disabled with a hint while nothing is selected |
| Existing
backups | Per row: id, creation time, file count, size, category tags, last verdict; actions are a *
*download** menu (one category or the manifest), **verify**, **preview restore**, **restore**, and *
*delete** (restore and delete take a second click to confirm; delete is the destructive-colored one)

|
| GitHub sync | Enable switch, `owner/repo`, branch, subdirectory, token environment variable, wh
ether a token was detected, and **push / pull** |

"Back up now" covers only the checked categories; saving the settings also makes that
selection the
default for scheduled runs.

Settings are written to the plugin's own user layer at
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-backup/settings.json` (

`0600`); the deployment baseline stays
in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and the two are shallow-m

yment baseline stays
in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and the two are shallow-merged (user wins).
## Layout on disk
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The manifest is written last and atomically, so "a directory with a manifest" is a
complete backup.

Intermediate files carry a `.part` suffix while a run is in
flight; residue from a crash is cleaned
up or ignored at the start of the next run.
## Categories and exclusions
| key | Sources (relative to `$DSH_HOME`) | Default |
| `settings` | `settings.yaml*`, `cordis.patch.yml*`, `.credentials.yaml*`, `.anonymous-user-id`, `d

sh-skill-hub.json`, `skills-market-sync.json` | on |
| `skills` | `skills-management/**` | on |
| `p
lugins` | `profiles/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `cordis.patch.yml*`, p

lus `plugins/**` | on |
| `sessions` | `sessions/**` | off |
| `storages` | `storages/**` | off |

Always excluded: `node_modules` and `.git*` at any depth, symbolic links, and the
backup root itself
— so keeping the store inside `$DSH_HOME` never recurses.
### Measured on a real harness home (`settings` + `plugins` + `skills`)
| Category | Files | Raw | Archive | Duration |

| `settings` | 5 | 2.0 KB | 1.3 KB | < 0.1 s |
| `plugins` | 39 | 1.24 MB | 1.12 MB | 0.2 s |

Creation and verification are streaming (flat memory; measured RSS went 57 MB →
158 MB), so a catego

ry is never held in memory. That is why the default ceiling is
**512 MiB**: a realistic skills tree

already passes 100 MiB compressed. Raise
`maxArchiveBytes` in the settings if yours is larger, or le

ave `skills` out and
back it up by hand. With retention 20 and `skills` enabled the store can reach

kills` out and
back it up by hand. With retention 20 and `skills` enabled the store can reach ~3 GB.
